hero.title: Governance and repository model
hero.lead: IATF keeps accessibility projects public, legible, and maintainable.
support: This page explains what qualifies, how repositories are held, and what repository-level responsibility applies after acceptance.

cards.title: Mission fit
paragraphs: IATF accepts work that addresses a real accessibility barrier and has clear public value.
A project should be useful beyond a single private workflow and workable as a public repository.

For web accessibility, IATF uses [W3C WAI](https://www.w3.org/WAI/) as its primary standards reference. The direct experience of users of assistive technologies is also practical evidence of what works in real use.

cards.title: Project acceptance
paragraphs: A proposal may be accepted when review shows that:
items: it addresses a real accessibility need
the problem is clear enough to evaluate
the scope is realistic enough to launch
the work aligns with the IATF mission
there is a plausible path to maintenance or completion

cards.title: Repository ownership
paragraphs: Accepted projects are created under the IATF GitHub organization.
Repositories stay there so each project keeps a stable public home, even if maintainers later change.

cards.title: Licensing
paragraphs: IATF projects use copyleft licensing unless a project states otherwise:

maintainer.title: Responsible engineer or maintainer
paragraphs: Each accepted project should have a named responsible engineer or maintainer. That person may receive admin access to the repository and is expected to:
items: review or manage issues and pull requests
keep the project understandable for others
maintainer.footnote: This is repository-level responsibility. Organizational ownership stays with IATF. Responsibility here is repository stewardship, technical direction, and public coordination — not unlimited private delivery, custom integrations, or service-level commitments outside the public roadmap.

publicDevelopment.title: Public development
paragraphs: Projects launched through IATF are developed in public by default. The repository is the public source of truth for:
publicDevelopment.footnote: Important project knowledge should not live only in private chats or inboxes.

paragraphs: LibreAccessibility keeps original proposals private in accesslibre/intake. Authorized reviewers use them to review accessibility barriers, reply and coordinate agreed work, not for marketing.

A public request record is a rewritten summary of the barrier, outcome and reasons, never a transcript. Remove unnecessary contact details, medical information and identifying context; removing names alone does not guarantee anonymity.

Before publishing a proposal summary, show the requester the exact text and obtain affirmative permission. Keep approval privately. Silence is not permission, and refusing publication does not affect review.

Record relevant Discord decisions without copying conversations or private proposal details. A public message is not permission to republish a proposal summary. Use private channels for private information.

Review active records at least annually. On closure, schedule a review 12 calendar months later and remove or genuinely anonymize personal data no longer needed, sooner where appropriate. Accepted projects do not automatically require keeping the full original form.

Relevant records may be kept longer for a documented ongoing need, legal obligation or legal claim, with restricted access and another review date. The applicable legal period must be justified; the lifetime of the organization is not a general retention period.

The proposal coordinator checks the private review register monthly. Reviews and removal are manual. The delivery service separately removes receipt metadata after 30 days; this does not remove proposal text from GitHub.

Request search-index exclusion where technically available, but do not treat it as access control or promise it on GitHub. LibreAccessibility can amend or remove records it controls, but cannot guarantee removal from third-party caches, forks, screenshots or notifications.

For access, correction, deletion or withdrawal of publication permission, email contact@libreaccessibility.org. The current policy is https://github.com/accesslibre/governance/blob/main/decisions/2026-006-proposal-privacy-and-retention.md and supersedes earlier IATF publication and indefinite-retention wording.

chair.lead: The chair holds organization-level stewardship of IATF. This is distinct from the per-project responsible engineer role: the chair is responsible for the organization as a whole, not for the day-to-day direction of any single repository.

duties.title: What the chair does
items: Holds owner permissions on the IATF GitHub organization
Signs off on project acceptance and archival decisions
Acts as the public point of contact for IATF
duties.footnote: The chair does not commit IATF to private delivery, paid work, or service-level agreements, and does not override per-repository maintainer decisions on technical direction.

election.title: Annual election
paragraphs: The chair is elected once a year. The election runs in the first two weeks of December, results are announced by December 15, and the new term begins on January 1.

Eligible voters are people who held a maintainer role on any IATF repository during the year and made at least one merged contribution to an IATF repository in that year. Each eligible voter has one vote. The candidate with the most votes wins; in the event of a tie, a runoff is held in the third week of December.
The election is run as a public GitHub Discussion in the designated IATF governance repository, so the candidates, the vote, and the result are all part of the public record.

continuity.title: Continuity
paragraphs: If no election is held in a given year, the current chair continues in the role until the next election. This is an indefinite continuation, not a grace period — the model is designed to keep the organization stable when activity is low, not to force a transition that nobody is ready for.
The chair may step down at any time. Active maintainers may also call an extraordinary election with a stated reason, run under the same rules as the annual election.

chair.footnote: The chair role was formalized in 2026 to make organization-level stewardship explicit. Until then, organizational responsibility was held informally by the founder.

states.title: Project states
paragraphs: Projects use a small set of public states:
states.footnote: These states keep the registry easy to scan.

reassignment.title: Reassignment and archiving
paragraphs: If a maintainer steps away or becomes inactive, IATF may reassign responsibility, pause development, or archive the project.
A project may also be archived when the original need has been met, maintenance has stopped, or continued work is no longer realistic.
reassignment.footnote: Archived projects remain publicly visible unless there is a compelling reason to do otherwise.

boundaries.footnote: IATF is a public repository model, not a private delivery service.
